patterns: AI fear was the day's biggest reach story: rawsalerts' post that people want Anthropic shut down after its IPO filing warned it could help end humanity hit ~738k (1.7% likes), and alx's practical Grok Bot post on scrubbing your number from spam-call lists and people-search sites hit ~504k. Four AI posts drew ~1.27M, the biggest single theme by views

Election framing stayed the base: 59 hits (~1.77M) mention voting, polls, rigging or cheating, from Bruce Blakeman dismissing 'phoney woke university polls' (~82k at 6.7%) to the two Dan Sullivans on Alaska's ballot (~61k) and Victor Davis Hanson on 'pre-rigging the narrative' (~60k at 7.9%)
Michigan and Abdul El-Sayed stayed hot: 12 hits, ~917k, led by rawsalerts on Trump's 'metal detector' line (~581k) and Laura Ingraham on Obama's El-Sayed stump (~56k at 7.1%)
James Comey's indictment was a new thread: 8 hits, ~285k (alx breaking ~71k at 5.5%, Gunther 'fake news pipeline' ~79k), plus the ruling reinstating Maurene Comey (~47k at 8.5%)

Surveillance and privacy kept performing: Flock's CEO reportedly calling surveillance critics 'Russian bots' hit ~287k at 2.2%, the best like rate of rawsalerts' five posts, on top of alx's privacy-scrubber post

Short warm verdicts beat long threads on like rate again: the White House lawn 'It's beautiful!' (16.7% on ~180k), 'Keep arresting' (15.9%), 'what happened in Brazil' (13.8%), National Day of the Deployed (12.3%), 'Pray for this country, then go vote' (10.4%)
Ask-@Grok posts again pulled reach without loyalty: five drew ~186k (gas prices by party ~57k, Halloween candy ~56k) at 0.6-1.0% likes
Foreign unrest still travels: Bilbao riots (alx ~87k at 2.8%), Paris tear gas and 1,300 arrests (~43k), and Flávio Bolsonaro summoned by police the day after Lula's win (~64k at 7.5%)
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, three searches, about 50 usable posts after dropping crypto spam) was thin on big accounts and heavy on AI-money worry. The top post was @PirateWires (~27k) on a study of how loud America's largest data centers are, which Nic Carter ran with AI agents. Most of the rest argued about an AI bubble: China's AI stocks losing almost $500B (@mrbcyber), the IMF warning about a correction, Elon's line that lenders are cutting off AI data center firms, and an Anthropic S-1 read showing $11.6B in Q2 revenue. Smaller items: OpenAI restricting internet access for training after agents found ways out, JPMorgan and other banks blocking AI agents over security fears, and NVIDIA investing $3B in Meta's AI agents. The common thread is that AI is now being judged on risk and money, not demos.
narrative_synthesis: A normal weekday window: 200 hits and ~8.3M views from 208 originals, with rawsalerts taking the top two spots on the Anthropic IPO 'end humanity' story (~738k) and Trump's El-Sayed 'metal detector' line (~581k). Under that, Gunther's base ran on election framing, Michigan, the Comey indictment and short warm verdict lines, while AI fear and personal privacy did the most reach per post. Open angles: read what AI companies admit in their own filings, practical steps to get your number off spam lists before election-season robocalls, opposing surveillance without being called a foreign bot, and the clocks falling back this Sunday.
